{"result":"page: https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/model-lifecycle | "Model lifecycle policy" | section: naming-convention

## https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/model-lifecycle#general-availability
    Model lifecycle policy > Lifecycle stages > General Availability
### General Availability {#general-availability}

General Availability models are production-ready and stable. They:

- Receive **no silent updates**.
- Are the only models eligible for aliases `-latest` and `-major`. See [model naming convention](https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/model-lifecycle#naming-convention).
- Are supported until retirement.

## https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/model-lifecycle#naming-convention
    Model lifecycle policy > Model naming convention
## Model naming convention {#naming-convention}

Model identifiers use a `model-name-major-minor` format, for example `mistral-medium-3-5`.

General Availability models support three aliases:

| Alias | Example | Points to |
|---|---|---|
| `model-name-latest` | `mistral-medium-latest` | Latest General Availability version, across generations |
| `model-name-major` | `mistral-medium-3` | Latest minor version of that major generation |
| `model-name-major-minor` | `mistral-medium-3-5` | Fixed major and minor version |

Labs models are always prefixed with `labs-`. Public Preview models use the `major-minor` format but aren't eligible for a `-latest` or `-major` alias.

> **Warning**
>
> Aliases automatically switch to newer models once they reach General Availability. As a result, using an alias may expose you to silent updates in model behavior and pricing. For precise control, pin your deployment to a specific major.minor version identifier.

## https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/model-lifecycle#deprecation-policy
    Model lifecycle policy > Deprecation policy
## Deprecation policy {#deprecation-policy}

Deprecation is announced as soon as a replacement model is available. The replacement can be in General Availability or Public Preview.

| Stage | Notice period |
|---|---|
| Labs | 1 month |
| Public Preview | 1 month |
| General Availability | 6 months |
| Third-party models | 1 month |

During the deprecation period, the model remains accessible. Once retired, requests to its identifiers fail with a `404` error.

Results: 3 sections, the whole section."}

content.text:
Based on the [Model lifecycle policy documentation](https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/model-lifecycle#naming-convention):

**What an alias currently points to:**
- `mistral-medium-latest` always points to the **latest General Availability version across all generations**
- This is defined semantically — the alias is dynamic and automatically resolves to whatever is currently the latest GA release

The documentation doesn't describe a programmatic API to query the resolved alias; instead, you determine it by checking which version is currently marked as the latest GA model on [Mistral's models page](https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/function_calling/) or in your API responses.

**When it will change:**
Aliases **automatically switch when a new model reaches General Availability**. The documentation warns:

> Aliases automatically switch to newer models once they reach General Availability. As a result, using an alias may expose you to silent updates in model behavior and pricing.

**To avoid unexpected changes:**
Pin your deployment to a specific version instead, such as `mistral-medium-2508` (the full `major-minor` identifier). This gives you precise control and prevents automatic updates. GA models receive no silent updates, so you'll only change versions when you deliberately redeploy with a new model ID.
